 LiveLaw Delhi High Court Weekly Round-Up: November 09 To November 15, 2026
 Nupur Thapliyal 
 16 Nov 2026 9:36 PM IST
 Share this 
 Listen to this Article Citations 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1071 to 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1087 
 NOMINAL INDEX

 Delhi High Court Takes Suo Motu Cognizance Of Unsafe Buildings, Orders Panel To Explore 'Controlled Demolition' Amid GRAP Restrictions 
 Case Title : Mohd Asif & Ors. v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1071
 The Delhi High Court has taken suo motu cognizance of the issue of dilapidated and structurally unsafe buildings in the national capital, observing that the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) cannot shirk away from its obligation by merely conducting inspections or issuing notices.
 Justice Saurabh Banerjee directed the MCD Commissioner, in consultation with the Chief Minister of Delhi, to constitute a High-Powered Committee to examine and formulate an effective alternative mechanism for dealing with buildings identified as dilapidated, structurally unsafe or dangerous during the ongoing Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) restrictions.
 Delhi High Court Rejects Plea To Remove Boxing Federation Of India President, Appoint Ad-Hoc Committee 
 Case Title : Delhi Amateur Boxing Association v. Union of India & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1072
 The Delhi High Court has dismissed a plea seeking to remove Ajay Singh as the President of the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) and to appoint an independent ad-hoc committee to oversee its administration.
 Delhi High Court Restrains US Copyright Suit Against TV Today Network Over Weather Footage In News Reports 
 Case Title : TV Today Network Limited v. Global Weather Productions LLC & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1073
 The Delhi High Court has restrained a US-based entity and some individuals from pursuing copyright infringement proceedings against TV Today Network before a US court, observing that the foreign proceedings were prima facie vexatious and oppressive as the dispute concerns news videos created and published in India for Indian audiences.
 Delhi High Court Dismisses Plea Seeking Rules To Address Misconduct By Airlines Staff 
 Case Title : Shalini Tiwari v. Union of India & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1074
 The Delhi High Court has dismissed a plea seeking directions to the Centre and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to frame specific rules and establish an effective mechanism for addressing misconduct, harassment and misbehaviour by airline personnel towards passengers.
 MCD & Police Must Ensure Chandni Chowk Remains Free Of Encroachments, Accessible To Pedestrians: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title : Chandni Chowk Sarv Vyapar Mandal (Regd.) v. Delhi Police Through Commissioner of Police & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1075
 The Delhi High Court has said that officials of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and Delhi Police must act in coordination to ensure that Chandni Chowk remains free from encroachments, accessible to pedestrians and conducive to the movement of visitors.
 Delhi High Court Flags Trend Of Disgruntled Litigants Casting Aspersions On Judges When Orders Go Against Them 
 Case Title : A v. B
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1076
 The Delhi High Court has flagged the trend of disgruntled litigants casting baseless aspersions against courts, judges and the judicial system when the outcome of legal proceedings is not in their favour.
 'Internet Wolves Operating In Packs': Delhi High Court Denies Anticipatory Bail To Man Accused Of ₹1 Crore Cyber Fraud 
 Case Title : Naseem Sheikh v. State of NCT of Delhi
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1077
 “Internet wolves, operating in packs, are increasingly on the prowl in cyberspace, acting in tandem and exploiting technology to defraud unsuspecting individuals,” the Delhi High Court has observed while highlighting the growing instances of organised cybercrime facilitated by the anonymity of the internet.
 Delhi High Court Seeks Timeline To Fill Vacancies In Child Rights Commission, Flags Overcrowding In Observation Homes 
 Case Title : Court On Its Own Motion v. Government of NCT of Delhi & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1078
 The Delhi High Court has sought a status report from the Delhi Government on vacancies in the Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR), while flagging that observation homes in the national capital are currently housing more than twice their sanctioned capacity.
 Delhi High Court Directs MCD To Prevent Recurrence Of Footpath Encroachments, Closes 10-Year-Old Contempt Case 
 Case Title : Parveen Kumar v. Alok KR Verma & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1079
 The Delhi High Court has directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and other concerned authorities to maintain vigilance and ensure that no projections or extensions from commercial establishments, or display of merchandise outside shops, encroach upon public footpaths.
 Spouse Can't Be Forced To Proceed With Mutual Divorce After Withdrawing Consent: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title : X v. Y
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1080
 The Delhi High Court has held that a spouse's decision to withdraw consent for divorce by mutual consent, even after entering into a mediated settlement agreement, cannot by itself constitute wilful disobedience warranting contempt proceedings.
 Earning Spouse, Married Children Or Siblings Not Automatically Disentitled To Motor Accident Compensation: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Savita & Anr.
 Citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1081
 The Delhi High Court has held that a married and earning daughter, son, spouse or sibling cannot be excluded from receiving compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act merely because they are married, financially independent or residing separately from the deceased.
 Justice Anish Dayal observed that the question of dependency in motor accident compensation cases must be determined on the basis of the facts and circumstances of each case, rather than by applying rigid classifications of dependants and non-dependants.
 Delhi High Court Enhances Compensation To ₹4.26 Crore For Road Accident Victim In Coma Since 2022 
 Case Title: BHARAT GHAI (THROUGH HIS WIFE HARPREET KAUR) v. RAJU GROVER (SINCE DECEASED) THROUGH HIS LRS & ANR. (BAJAJ ALLIANZ GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD.)
 Citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1082
 The Delhi High Court has enhanced the compensation payable to a 39-year-old man who was left in a comatose state with 100% permanent physical impairment following a road accident in February 2022.
 'Deplorable': Delhi High Court Slaps ₹1 Lakh Costs On Delhi Govt For Disregarding Court Orders, Directs Recovery From Officers' Salaries 
 Case Title: Central Footwear Co. v. Government of NCT of Delhi & Anr
 Citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1083
 The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of Rs. 1 lakh on the Delhi Government for repeatedly disregarding its earlier orders directing authorities to process an industrial unit's application for allotment of an alternative industrial plot under the 1996 Relocation Scheme.
 Justice Amit Mahajan directed the Delhi Government to pay the costs to the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee within six weeks.
 Delhi High Court Imposes ₹2 Lakh Costs On 'Serial Litigant', Bars Listing Of Fresh Cases Until Payment 
 Case Title Satya Prakash Ravidas v. The SDM/Registrar of Societies & Anr
 Citation 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1084
 The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of Rs. 2 lakh on a litigant for repeatedly approaching the Court seeking an inquiry into the affairs of a society and cancellation of its registration, despite similar reliefs having been rejected in earlier proceedings.
 Sexual Offence Victim's Identity Can't Be Disclosed Merely Because Accused Was Not Summoned For Rape: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title X v. HIGH COURT OF DELHI & ORS
 Citation 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1085
 The Delhi High Court has observed that the protection under Section 228A of the Indian Penal Code against disclosure of the identity of a sexual offence victim attaches to the allegation itself, and is not dependent on whether the accused was summoned for the offence.
 Victim's Wish To Live With Accused Can't Justify Quashing POCSO Case: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title : Salman Ahamad v. State (NCT of Delhi) & Ors
 CITATION : 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1086
 The Delhi High Court has held that a victim's wish to continue living with an accused and her family's acceptance of their relationship cannot override the statutory protections under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
 Longstanding Practice Of Organising Chhath Puja Can't Justify Use Of Public Green Area: Delhi High Court 
 Case Title Lalit Anand v. Government of NCT of Delhi & Ors
 Citation 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1087
 The Delhi High Court has observed that longstanding practice of organising Chhath Puja at a particular location cannot, by itself, justify permitting the use of a public green area for the religious festivities.
